body: This is on [Spooky Express](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=express.spooky&hl=en-US), but @AdriaandeJongh shared a screenshot of a similar bug on [Rift Riff](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.adriaandejongh.riftriff&hl=en-US). Adriaan, could you reshare it here and provide info about which device reproduces it? *Edit:* I grabbed the relevant info from the [#android RC channel](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/android?msg=vafiZpfEki8cDdRko): Seen on Galaxy Z Fold 6 and Nothing Phone 3. --- @torcado194 has a Nothing Phone 3a and can reproduce the glitch reliably on Spooky Express, so if @godotengine/rendering folks have hints for what to test, they might be able to help. (https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/releases/tag/4.5.1.stable%2Bvulkan_mobile_fixes)

Okay, then one possibility is the use of subpasses. We would need to test both with and without the separate post processing pass. To do that, it should be as simple as removing the WorldEnvironemnt and any camera effects, as well as ensuring that 3D scale is not used in the project settings

- OnePlus 13R: Adreno 750
- Nothing Phone 3a: Adreno 810
- Galaxy Z Fold6: Adreno 750

Not a lot of known affected devices yet to draw clear conclusions but this might be Adreno specific.

It tested on a Xiaomi Pocophone F1 (Adreno 630) and don't reproduce the issue there (only tested Spooky Express), but it's a much older and lower-end device with a different Adreno gen, and much older drivers. So the issue might be Adreno 7xx/8xx only.
I can't reproduce this on the MRP from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115217#issuecomment-3781014099 on a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra (Adreno 830, Android 16) with 4.6.rc2.

I just tested minimal MRP like torcado's MRP above with a Samsung Z Fold 7 (Adreno 830) and I can't reproduce the issue either. So I strongly suspect that we are seeing something that was fixed in a more recent driver update.

~@torcado194 If you start from that very minimal MRP, can try the following one at a time and then all together:
1. Turning on FXAA
2. Turning on Glow
3. Adding a transparent object to the scene~

Actually nevermind, I just noticed that your MRP is using the Forward+ renderer. So those things won't make much difference

@clayjohn these changes *did* make a difference

1. Turning on FXAA removed the issue
2. Turning on Glow removed the issue (via the Camera3D's environment with `glow` enabled, no other changes are necessary (except color changes to make the cube visible))
3. Adding a transparent object did not remove the issue (via an additional cube with a StandardMaterial3D with transparency set to Alpha, and Albedo set to a transparent white)
@torcado194 Was that with the Forward+ renderer still? Could you also test with the mobile renderer?

yes, this is with the editor is set to Forward+.
When I change the editor renderer to Mobile, it does not change the result of these tests.
To be clear, `rendering/renderer/rendering_method.mobile` is set to `mobile` by default. Just to make sure, I forced the `.mobile` renderer to `forward_plus`, which removes the issue altogether in the MRP. None of the additional changes make a difference

So far this tells us that the issue is potentially in the way that Adreno handles subpasses. I suspect that there is a synchronization error when the post processing pass uses a subpass and that results in values being read from the 3D texture before 3D rendering has finished.

I encountered the same issue on my Fairphone 6.  I launched claude on it and it was able to narrow down precisly when the  glitch happends, concluded that Godot was not at fault, and produced a minimal Vulkan app that has the same issue. I wanted to bug report this to Qualcomm, but I cannot sign in into the Qualcomm forums (it ask me for a country and then errors, idk if this is region block or just a bug). Here is the full claude report:

> Root cause narrowed with a standalone Vulkan reproducer (no Godot).
> 
> On an Adreno 810 (Fairphone 6, driver 512.800.53) the corruption needs exactly
> two conditions:
> 
> 1. the render area is **exactly** the presented surface's size - one pixel either
>    way in either axis is clean (59 sizes swept, only the display size corrupts);
> 2. the render pass **reads back its colour attachment** - alpha blending, or a
>    subpass input attachment.
> 
> One draw call is enough, and it is deterministic per configuration, not flaky.
> 
> This unifies the 2D and 3D reports, which never fitted one rule before: to a
> tiler, blending and an input-attachment read are the same thing - a tile
> read-modify-write. 2D corrupts because canvas items are blended; Forward Mobile
> corrupts because the post-process subpass reads the colour attachment, which is
> why disabling that subpass fixes 3D while resizing does not. MSAA fixes both
> because it changes the tile/resolve path.
> 
> Damage is whole 16x4 blocks (UBWC block size at 32bpp) at horizontal tile
> boundaries, spaced inversely to framebuffer width (320 rows at 1116px wide, 160
> at 2484px), only in tiles containing geometry.
> 
> Godot's Vulkan usage is not at fault: the corrupting frames produce zero errors
> and zero hazards under VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation with synchronization
> validation enabled, and a ~350-line standalone Vulkan app doing one blended draw
> into a correctly created offscreen image reproduces it identically. Filing with
> Qualcomm; reproducer (source + 40KB APK) attached. I could not find an existing
> Qualcomm ticket or Android tracker entry for this, so it appears unreported.
> 
> Workarounds for affected projects, any one is sufficient:
> - MSAA 2x (`rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_2d` or `msaa_3d`)
> - stretch mode `viewport` at a size != the device resolution
> - `rendering/scaling_3d/scale` < 1.0 for 3D
> - the Compatibility renderer
> 
> If a gated workaround is wanted in-engine, note that padding the render *area*
> avoids it losslessly in 2D (present the native sub-rect 1:1), but does not help
> 3D, where the subpass read is the trigger.

And the test Vulkan app: [vulkan-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31528898/vulkan-repro.zip)
